title: Mochi Parade — Illustrated Dessert Specimen
description: A warm-cream menu slide built around a row of hand-drawn mochi orbs — each a flavor specimen in matcha, strawberry, and taro — anchored by a brushy-serif café wordmark at top center. Entirely illustration-driven with zero photography and no hard geometric structure.
philosophy: This template believes food should be drawn, not photographed — that illustration carries a warmth and craft no camera can replicate. It exists for small dessert shops that lead with personality over polish, and it flatly refuses drop shadows, stock imagery, and corporate grid logic. Its design language is organic roundness, soft ink, and playful label typography. The room it belongs in is a pastel-lit café counter, not a slide deck conference call.
goodFor: Seasonal café menu boards with 4–6 illustrated flavor items
Social media product-reveal posts for dessert or boba shops
Brand identity slides for cute Japanese or Korean food businesses
Pop-up market menus where illustration replaces photography
avoidFor: Corporate investor pitch decks requiring data credibility
Photography-driven food lookbooks or editorial shoots
Dense multi-column text layouts with more than three sections
author: harness

examples.promptCore: This title slide should feel like the front cover of a beloved neighborhood café's hand-illustrated seasonal menu — warm, artisan, and quietly delightful without trying too hard. The mochi illustration row is the compositional hero; the title text exists only to frame it, never to compete. Overall mood is soft-ink craftsmanship: organic roundness, slightly imperfect linework, full of handmade personality. Avoid rigid symmetry-for-its-own-sake, any corporate polish, harsh outlines, or anything that reads as manufactured rather than lovingly drawn.

examples.layoutNotes: Single-column, center-anchored layout on a warm-cream field; the brushy title wordmark claims the top-center third of the slide with generous vertical breathing room beneath it. A horizontal parade of three hand-drawn mochi orbs spans the lower two-thirds, spaced evenly from margin to margin with hand-lettered flavor labels nested directly under each orb. A short subtitle tagline occupies a tight mid-band bridging the wordmark and the illustration row, kept to one or two lines. No hard outer border or rule lines — organic, margin-light edges allow the illustrated elements to feel discovered rather than contained.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a hand-lettered café chalkboard translated into soft pastel warmth — handmade, unhurried, and unapologetically cute. Three illustrated orbs hold the stage in a relaxed parade, each a self-contained flavor specimen with its own ink personality; the breathing room between them feels intentional, like pauses in a spoken menu. The overall mood is craft-counter intimacy — personal and tactile rather than retail-polished. Avoid hard geometric borders, drop shadows, or any framing device that implies a corporate grid; let ink outline and gentle fill do all the structural work.

examples.layoutNotes: The slide is built around a loose horizontal specimen band centered vertically, where three illustrated mochi orbs are spaced with generous organic gaps — not mechanically equal, but rhythmically balanced like objects arranged by hand on a counter. Each orb anchors a small flavor-label cluster directly beneath it: name on one line, a short tasting note or price tag below that, in a tight two-line stack. A single brushy category header sits flush-center above the row with ample sky between it and the orbs. No footer band, no page number, no bounding boxes — the outer edges dissolve into bare cream ground.
